domain_name: Platform & Trust: authentication, privilege, tenant isolation, audit, encryption, privacy operations and the Control Plane
summary: PLT makes Nabd safe to hold real patient data and keeps it that way: a PIN alone can no longer reach a session, break-glass and delegation cannot escalate privileges, RLS is enforced by the database with a migrator/runtime role split, every PHI read is logged and the audit chain is verified nightly, field encryption moves to per-tenant regional keys, patients can exercise DPDP rights before 13 May 2027, and the operator Control Plane becomes its own PHI-free service before the second cell. 63 stories in 8 epics, 478 estimate days; the 59 in-scope tracker tasks (Auth, Tenancy, Platform, Audit & privacy) carry 437 tracker days, plus 36 days for three control-plane tasks filed under Owner admin (T-087, T-123, T-207), so 473 tracker days against 478 planned. Phase 0 (P0) is 19 stories / 102 days and must pass before any real patient data enters any environment (doc06 Sprint 2 gate).

stories.title: Only full access tokens open the API: separate token types and audiences
stories.story: As a clinic owner responsible for patient data, I want challenge and purpose tokens to be useless as bearer credentials so that a stolen or guessed PIN can never bypass MFA.
stories.context: Today every token AuthService mints (staff access, mfa_pending, mfa_setup_required, step_up), OwnerService's owner_pending_workspace and PlatformAuthService's operator tokens are signed by the same key and accepted by the resource server (SecurityConfig.java:94). SessionRevocationJwtDecoder passes through any token without sid+tenantId, so an mfa_pending token issued after the PIN step reaches MFA enrol, break-glass activate and unlock (MF-01, Critical). The fix adds a mandatory `typ` claim (access | mfa_pending | mfa_setup | step_up | owner_select) and an `aud` claim (staff-api | platform-api | mfa | step-up | owner-select) to every mint site, makes the resource-server decoder accept only typ=access, and decodes challenge tokens only inside the controller that consumes them with a dedicated decoder. Every non-public endpoint must also see either a `sid` claim or a granted authority. Tokens minted before the deploy lack `typ` and are rejected; access tokens live 15 minutes and refresh still works, so users see at most one silent refresh. This is a prerequisite for break-glass gating (PLT-012), MFA hardening (PLT-004/005) and ADR-08.
acceptance: Given a staff member with MFA enabled who has entered a correct PIN, when the returned mfa_pending token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to any of the authenticated endpoints, then every call returns 401 (TokenMisuseMatrixTest enumerates all request mappings).
Given an mfa_pending challenge token, when it is posted to /v1/auth/mfa/verify with a valid TOTP, then a token pair with typ=access, aud=staff-api and a sid is returned.

Given a step_up token or an owner_select token, when used as a bearer token, then 401; when sent in X-Step-Up-Token to a step-up-protected action, then it is accepted only if its sub matches the caller.
Given a token without a typ claim (minted before the deploy), when presented, then 401 and the client's single-flight refresh obtains a new typed token without sending the user to /login.
Given an authenticated endpoint with no @PreAuthorize (/v1/auth/logout, /v1/auth/sessions, /v1/owners/me/workspaces), when called with a typ=access token lacking sid, then 401.
Given the CI pipeline, when any new controller method is added, then TokenMisuseMatrixTest discovers it automatically and fails the build if a non-access token is accepted.

stories.title: Signing keys survive deploys: keys from the secret manager, JWKS with two active kids
stories.story: As a receptionist I want to stay signed in when Nabd deploys or restarts a server so that a release in the middle of the morning rush never logs the desk out.
stories.context: config/JwtConfig.java generates a fresh RSA-2048 key pair with a random kid on every boot (MF-13). Every deploy logs everybody out, a second replica rejects the first replica's tokens, there is no JWKS, and iss/aud are not validated. The fix loads the signing keys from the cell's secret manager (KMS-protected), publishes a JWKS containing the active and the next/previous kid so rotation overlaps, and validates iss/aud/typ on every decode. The dev profile may still generate an ephemeral key, but the prod profile fails to boot without configured keys. This unblocks two replicas behind a load balancer (Phase 0 exit gate) and the separate issuers in PLT-009.
acceptance: Given two replicas behind the load balancer, when a user signs in on replica A and the next request lands on replica B, then it succeeds (restart/refresh test QA-37).

Given a rolling restart of both replicas, when a signed-in receptionist keeps working, then nobody is logged out and no request returns 401 except a normal 15-minute expiry followed by a silent refresh.
Given GET /.well-known/jwks.json, then it returns exactly 2 active keys (current and next/previous kid) and no private material.
Given a token with the wrong iss, wrong aud, unknown kid or missing typ, then decode fails with 401.
Given SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod and no JWT key configuration, when the app boots, then startup fails with a clear error naming the missing secret.
Given the rotation runbook, when the next key is promoted, then tokens signed with the previous kid stay valid until they expire (overlap >= refresh TTL of the access token, 15 min).

stories.title: Brute-force limits on TOTP and unlock, 6-digit PINs, and a client IP that cannot be forged
stories.story: As a receptionist on a shared desk PC I want my account protected against someone guessing my PIN or authenticator code so that nobody can sign in as me.
stories.context: TOTP verification (AuthService.verifyMfa, issueStepUpToken, confirmMfa) has no attempt counter, so once a PIN is known the second factor can be guessed across re-issued challenges (MF-09). /v1/auth/unlock is an unthrottled PIN oracle, PINs are 4-6 digits, and RequestMeta.clientIp() returns the first X-Forwarded-For value, so the per-IP throttle (20/min) and audit IPs can be forged and a malformed header causes a 500 on the ::inet cast (MF-10). The fix counts failed PIN, OTP, TOTP, unlock and recovery-code attempts per account in `login_attempts` and drives the existing exponential lockout (capped at 30 min, non-renewing) from all of them; adds TOTP replay protection (a used time-step cannot be reused); raises the PIN policy to 6-8 digits with a forced change at next login for shorter PINs; and derives the client IP from Tomcat's RemoteIpValve with a trusted-proxy list. Owner and operator passphrases are behind a decision (see risks).
acceptance: Given an account with a known PIN, when 5 wrong TOTP codes are submitted across any number of fresh challenges, then the account is locked with the same backoff as PIN failures and further correct codes are refused until the lock expires (TotpLockoutTest).
Given /v1/auth/unlock, when 5 wrong PINs are posted, then the session is locked and the 6th attempt returns 423 without verifying the PIN (UnlockBruteForceTest).
Given a valid TOTP code already used for a sign-in, when it is replayed within its 30 s window, then it is rejected.

Given a staff member whose PIN has 4 or 5 digits, when they sign in successfully, then they must set a 6-8 digit PIN before any other call succeeds; invite accept and PIN reset reject PINs shorter than 6 digits with 400.
Given a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` from a non-trusted hop, then rate limits and the audit_log ip_address use the real peer address (XffSpoofTest).
Given `X-Forwarded-For: not-an-ip`, then the request never returns 500 and the audit row stores the validated peer IP.

stories.title: MFA re-enrolment needs the current factor, recovery codes work, and an owner can reset a lost authenticator
stories.story: As a doctor who lost my phone I want to sign in once with a recovery code, and have my owner reset my authenticator safely, so that I am not locked out of my clinic and nobody else can silently replace my MFA.
stories.context: MFA re-enrolment overwrites the active secret without proof of the current factor, recovery codes accumulate on every enrolment and are never consumed (consumeRecoveryCode has no caller), and there is no admin reset (MF-08). The fix stores a pending secret alongside the active one, so the old secret keeps working until the new one is confirmed; re-enrolment of an enabled account requires the current TOTP or a step-up token; confirming rotates the recovery-code set (old unused codes are revoked); the MFA challenge accepts a single-use recovery code; and an owner (staff:edit + step-up) can reset another staff member's MFA, which is audited, revokes that person's sessions and forces enrolment at next sign-in. Operators get the same flow on master.operators.
acceptance: Given an enabled authenticator, when the user starts re-enrolment without the current TOTP or a step-up token, then 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED and the active secret is unchanged.
Given re-enrolment started, when the user signs in before confirming, then the old authenticator still works (pending secret is not active).
Given confirmation of a new secret, then exactly 8 new recovery codes are shown once and all previously unused codes stop working.
Given an MFA challenge, when a valid recovery code is submitted, then the session is issued, the code is marked used and cannot be reused, and the owner sees an audit entry 'recovery code used'.
Given an owner with step-up, when they reset a doctor's MFA, then an audit row `staff.mfa_reset` is written, the doctor's sessions are revoked within 60 s and the next sign-in forces enrolment.
Given a receptionist (no staff:edit), when they call the reset endpoint, then 403.

stories.title: MFA is mandatory for owners, money approvers and every Nabd operator
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want my own account, anyone who can refund or approve money, and every Nabd operator to be forced through MFA so that the most powerful accounts can never be PIN-only.
stories.context: MFA is driven by the per-role boolean roles.mfa_required (AuthService.mfaRequiredByPolicy ~L139-142). Nothing forces it on for the built-in Owner role, roles holding billing:refundDiscount or any :approve authority, platform operators (PlatformAuthService only checks operators.mfa_enabled ~L91, including super_admin) or owner accounts, which have no MFA at all (MF-12). The fix computes an MfaPolicy invariant from the effective grants: required when the role is built-in Owner, contains refundDiscount or approve on any module, or the identity is an operator or owner account. It cannot be switched off by role edits or config in prod. Accounts in scope without MFA are routed into enrolment (mfa_setup token) at next sign-in. Owner accounts (OwnerService two-step login) get TOTP enrolment and a challenge before workspace selection. FRD NFR-06 allows WhatsApp OTP as the second factor for small clinics; the policy object supports 'totp' now and 'whatsapp_otp' behind a decision.
acceptance: Given a staff member whose role is built-in Owner, or whose grants include billing:refundDiscount or any :approve, and MFA is not enrolled, when they enter a correct PIN, then they receive only an mfa_setup token and cannot reach any other endpoint until enrolment is confirmed.
Given an owner edits such a role and sets mfa_required=false, then the API returns 422 MFA_REQUIRED_BY_POLICY.
Given any platform operator (support, sre, compliance_dpo, super_admin) without MFA, when they sign in, then they are forced into enrolment; super_admin cannot be exempted.
Given an owner account (OwnerService login), when the PIN is correct, then a TOTP challenge is required before /v1/owners/workspaces/select issues a workspace token.
Given SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod and app.auth.mfa.enforce-privileged=false, when the app boots, then startup fails.
Given the staff list, then each row shows MFA status and the platform tenant view shows % of privileged users enrolled (target 100%).

stories.title: OTP requests are limited per phone number and never reveal whether a number exists
stories.story: As the Nabd platform team I want OTP sends limited per phone number with a silent response so that nobody can pump paid WhatsApp/SMS messages or discover which numbers are registered.
stories.context: POST /v1/auth/otp/request has no per-number limit (MF-24 S2 part); only the forgeable per-IP limit applies, which enables message pumping (each OTP costs a WhatsApp authentication template) and account enumeration through response differences. The fix adds a Postgres counter keyed by an HMAC of the normalised phone number (no raw phone stored) with SYS-01 rules: at most 3 sends per 15 minutes and 10 per 24 hours per number, resend no sooner than 60 s, and a per-tenant hourly cap. The endpoint always returns 202 with the same body and similar latency whether the number exists, is limited, or is unknown. PLT-008 later moves the counters to Valkey token buckets; this Postgres version is the Phase 0 control and the fallback if Valkey is unavailable.
acceptance: Given a phone number that received 3 OTPs in the last 15 minutes, when a 4th is requested, then no message is sent and the response is still 202 with the standard body.
Given an unknown phone number, when an OTP is requested, then the response is 202 with the same body as for a known number and the p95 latency difference is < 50 ms.
Given a resend within 60 s of the previous send, then no message is sent and the response is 202.

Given a pumping script that rotates 1,000 numbers against one tenant within an hour, then sends stop at the per-tenant cap (default 200/h, configurable per plan) and an alert is raised to the platform team.
Given the otp_send_counters table, then it contains no raw phone numbers (HMAC only) and rows older than 48 h are purged.

stories.title: Sessions end when they should: suspension, role change, operator logout and a 12-hour cap
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want suspending a staff member, changing their role, or suspending the clinic to end their sessions within a minute so that access stops the moment I decide it should.
stories.context: Revocation has gaps (MF-60): operator tokens carry sid but no tenantId so SessionRevocationJwtDecoder skips the liveness check; tenant suspension/offboarding (TenantLifecycleService ~L44-56) revokes nothing; refresh() and owner workspace select do not check tenant status; PATCH /v1/staff/{id} role changes do not revoke; refresh rotation gives a fresh 30-day expiry forever (no absolute lifetime); and step-up tokens are not bound to the session or tenant. The fix checks operator tokens against master.sessions, revokes all tenant sessions on suspension/offboarding, rejects refresh and workspace select for non-active tenants, revokes a staff member's sessions on any role/scope/field-grant change, caps each refresh family at about one shift (12 h, configurable per tenant later by SSO policy), and binds step-up tokens to sid and tenantId. Revocations publish an event so open tabs are signed out via SSE.
acceptance: Given an operator who logs out, when their access token is used 10 s later, then 401 (liveness checked against master.sessions).

Given a tenant moved to suspended or offboarded, then every staff session in that tenant is revoked within 60 s, refresh returns 401 TENANT_INACTIVE and owner workspace select returns 403 TENANT_INACTIVE.
Given an owner changes a receptionist's role or scope, then the receptionist's open tabs are signed out within 60 s and the next sign-in carries the new permissions.
Given a refresh family started 12 h ago, when refresh is attempted, then 401 SESSION_MAX_AGE and the user signs in again (idle-lock unlock does not extend the cap).
Given a step-up token minted in session A, when presented with session B's access token, then 403 STEP_UP_INVALID.
Given suspension of one staff member via one tap, then all their sessions on all devices end (NB-047).

stories.title: Rate limits per tenant, user, phone and IP that hold across replicas
stories.story: As the Nabd platform team I want token-bucket rate limits per tenant, user, phone and IP shared across replicas so that one abusive client or tenant cannot degrade every clinic's morning rush.
stories.context: Rate limits cover auth only and the per-IP counter was forgeable (MF-24 S3 part, NB-288). With Valkey in-region (T-080, Data & Infra), this story adds Bucket4j-style token buckets in Valkey keyed `rl:{dim}:{id}`: per tenant for the whole API (default 600 req/min, burst 1,200, raised per plan), per user/session (120 req/min), per IP for pre-auth and public endpoints (20 req/min), and per phone HMAC for OTP (migrating PLT-006 rules). Limits return 429 Problem+JSON with Retry-After, except OTP endpoints, which stay silent 202. If Valkey is unavailable the tenant/user limits fail open with an alert, while OTP limits fall back to the Postgres counter from PLT-006 (fail closed). Patient Access Edge applies the same library at its own ingress.

Given OTP requests over the per-number limit, then the response is still 202 and nothing is sent.
Given Valkey is stopped, then API calls continue (tenant/user limits fail open, alert fires within 2 min) and OTP limits are enforced from Postgres.
Given a plan with a higher API quota (PLT-059), then the tenant bucket uses the plan's limit within 60 s of the plan change.

stories.title: Break-glass is an eligible clinician's 30-minute, read-only emergency access that the owner hears about at once
stories.story: As an emergency doctor I want to open a patient's record in an emergency outside my normal scope with one justified, step-up-confirmed action, and as the owner I want to be told within a minute, so that emergencies are never blocked but break-glass is never a back door to Owner rights.
stories.context: POST /v1/auth/break-glass/activate has no @PreAuthorize (AuthController ~L126-130); any authenticated caller, including an mfa_pending token, gets the tenant's full built-in Owner grant set folded into a new token for 30 minutes (AuthService.mintTokenPair ~L560-572 via repo.findBuiltInOwnerRole), and can then create a 30-day self-delegation. Deactivate is also ungated (MF-02, SEC-36). The fix adds a dedicated `clinical:breakGlass` authority (new ModuleGrant action, seeded only for Doctor, Owner-doctor and ER roles), requires a step-up token with purpose break_glass, requires a reason code plus free text (text stored, never logged), replaces the Owner grant merge with a fixed BREAK_GLASS_GRANTS set (clinical:view, patients:view; no create/edit/delete/approve/staff), lets the token bypass own-patients and department scoping for reads only, hard-expires at 30 minutes, and notifies every Owner in-app and on WhatsApp (no PHI in the body) within 60 s. Deactivate is limited to the grant holder or staff:edit (quick win #11). Break-glass v2 (per-patient Cedar context flag, ADR-08) replaces the scope later.
acceptance: Given a receptionist, when they call break-glass activate, then 403 (BreakGlassAuthzTest).

Given a doctor with clinical:breakGlass but no step-up token, then 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED; with a valid step-up token and reason code, then 201 and a token whose permissions are exactly the base grants plus clinical:view and patients:view (no staff:edit, no billing, no :approve).

Given an activation, then every Owner of the tenant receives an in-app alert and a WhatsApp utility message ('Emergency access used by <staff name> at <time>. Review in Nabd.') within 60 s, with no patient name or diagnosis.

Given the break-glass token, when a write endpoint (POST/PATCH/DELETE on clinical, staff, roles, billing) is called, then 403; a clinical GET on a patient outside own-patients scope succeeds and is logged with purpose break_glass (PLT-039).
Given 30 minutes after activation, then the grant is expired, the elevated session is revoked and further calls with that token return 401 (J14).
Given a staff member who is not the holder and lacks staff:edit, when they deactivate someone else's grant, then 403.

stories.title: Nobody can delegate rights to themselves or pass on rights they only borrowed
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want delegations to be granted only by someone else, only from their own permanent role, so that no one can turn a temporary or emergency right into a 30-day Owner role.

stories.title: RLS is real: migrator owns the tables, the app runs as a NOBYPASSRLS role, every tenant table has forced per-command policies, and boot fails otherwise
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want the database itself to refuse to show or change another clinic's rows, even if application code forgets a tenant filter, so that one bug cannot leak my patients' data.
stories.context: Flyway runs as the app user (application.yml has no spring.flyway.user; Dockerfile and scripts/dev-up.sh migrate at app boot), so nabd_app owns every table and Postgres skips RLS for owners; no table has FORCE RLS; no policy has an explicit WITH CHECK; and login_attempts, workflow_definitions, package_eligible_doctors, owners, brands, legal_entities and tax_registrations have no RLS (MF-03 Critical, MF-63). Tests pass only because ApiTestBase migrates as superuser and connects as a different role. The fix: a roles bootstrap (nabd_migrator owns schemas and runs Flyway as a separate job; nabd_app is DML-only NOBYPASSRLS with statement_timeout 5s, lock_timeout 3s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 15s; nabd_reports read-only; nabd_definer owns SECURITY DEFINER functions); a generated migration that sets FORCE RLS and replaces each USING-only policy with ADR-07 per-command policies on every tenant table (the 20 brand-widened tables are handled in PLT-018); RLS for the remaining tables (workflow_definitions allows tenant_id IS NULL rows for read only; package_eligible_doctors gains tenant_id; owner PIN hashes become reachable only through SECURITY DEFINER functions); and an RlsInvariantVerifier that fails application start if the runtime role owns a tenant table, has BYPASSRLS, or any tenant_id table lacks forced RLS or a WITH CHECK policy. The prod-config CI job (T-020, QA) boots exactly this topology.
acceptance: Given the deployed topology, then `SELECT relname FROM pg_class WHERE relowner = 'nabd_app'::regrole` returns no rows and nabd_app has rolbypassrls = false (RlsSchemaInvariantTest).

Given every table in public with a tenant_id column, then relrowsecurity and relforcerowsecurity are true and pg_policies shows a SELECT policy and INSERT/UPDATE policies with WITH CHECK (or the table is listed in an explicit, reviewed exemption file).
Given the app connects as a role that owns a tenant table or has BYPASSRLS, when it boots, then startup fails with a message naming the offending table or role.
Given a repository query that omits the tenant predicate, when run under tenant A's context, then it returns only tenant A's rows; an INSERT with tenant B's tenant_id fails with an RLS violation.
Given scripts/dev-up.sh, then local development runs Flyway as nabd_migrator and the app as nabd_app, and the existing 560 RLS tests are green under that topology.
Given the CI prod-config job (T-020), then Flyway runs as migrator, the app as nabd_app, and the suite passes.

stories.title: Contain brand-visibility widening and switch to the fast array policy
stories.story: As a clinic owner in a group I want sibling clinics unable to read or write my patients through a database setting, and as a receptionist I want check-in to stay fast, so that sharing happens only with consent and the morning queue never stalls.
stories.context: TenantContext.set populates app.accessible_tenant_ids from brands.data_visibility_scope, and 20 tables (patients, staff, sessions, roles, appointments, queue_entries, consents, patient_merges, doctor_working_hours, doctor_leave, clinical_notes and nine setup tables in V6, V17, V19) use OR-shaped USING policies with no WITH CHECK: reads widen without consent, writes into siblings are allowed, TENANT scope is unilateral, and the OR defeats indexes (nextTokenNumber 933 ms inside the check-in lock) (MF-04 Critical, CONS §7 M0/M1). This story runs CONS M0 (inventory of brands with scope <> FACILITY and owner contact) and M1: rewrites the 20 policies to the ADR-07 per-command form (indexable `tenant_id = ANY(uuid[])` read, single-tenant WITH CHECK), removes widening on staff, sessions and roles unconditionally, and makes TenantContext set app.visible_tenant_ids to the single tenant unless the `nabd.legacy-brand-visibility` flag is on and the brand is on an allow-list (default off). It also adds explicit tenant_id predicates to QueueRepository.nextTokenNumber, ScheduleRepository.countSessionOccupancy, the PatientRepository registry subqueries and AuthRepository lookups.

stories.title: Tenant context is bound when a transaction starts and can never silently change
stories.story: As an engineer on any module I want the tenant to be bound automatically from the signed-in user at transaction start, and any attempt to switch it mid-transaction to fail loudly, so that I cannot introduce a cross-tenant bug by forgetting or misusing TenantContext.
stories.context: TenantContext.set is called by hand at about 240 sites, nothing asserts a transaction is active, and AuditService.record calls TenantContext.set(tenantId) inside the caller's transaction, silently replacing app.tenant_id for the rest of it (MF-62, ARCH-19, SEC-32). A forgotten call today fails closed (no rows) only by luck of set_config semantics. The fix binds the tenant from the SecurityContext (JWT tenantId) when a Spring-managed transaction begins (TransactionSynchronization on a tenant-aware DataSource), makes TenantContext.set throw if no transaction is active or if a different tenant is already bound, makes AuditService assert the tenant is unchanged, and provides an explicit TenantScope.run(tenantId, ...) API for workers and system jobs. @CurrentTenant/@CurrentStaff argument resolvers replace tenantId(Jwt) helpers; the tenantId parameters are removed module by module by S6. This unblocks every squad and the Modulith boundary work.
acceptance: Given a repository call on an RLS table outside a transaction, then it throws IllegalStateException in tests and is flagged by an ArchUnit rule.
Given a request authenticated for tenant A, when a @Transactional service method starts, then app.tenant_id and app.visible_tenant_ids are already set to A without any explicit call.
Given a transaction bound to tenant A, when code calls TenantContext.set(B) or AuditService.record(B, ...), then it throws TenantMismatchException and the transaction rolls back.
Given a worker job (outbox handler, ETA engine), then it must use TenantScope.run(tenantId, ...) and an ArchUnit rule forbids TenantContext.set outside shared/tenancy.
Given the codebase at S6, then the count of explicit tenantId method parameters on service methods has dropped to 0 in modules migrated so far (CI metric reported per sprint).

stories.title: Composite tenant foreign keys on the clinical spine
stories.story: As an engineer I want foreign keys that include tenant_id so that a row in clinic A can never reference clinic B's patient, staff member or visit, even if an id is replayed.
stories.context: Single-column foreign keys are checked by Postgres without RLS, so tenant A can insert a row referencing tenant B's patient or staff id (MF-64, DP-18, QA-28). The fix adds UNIQUE (tenant_id, id) on parent tables (patients, staff, queue_entries, appointments, invoices, prescriptions, clinical_notes, departments) and replaces child FKs on the clinical spine with composite (tenant_id, x_id) FKs: vitals, clinical_notes, prescriptions, patient_allergies, chronic_conditions, clinical_documents, vaccine_records, dental_chart_entries, queue_entries, appointments, invoices, consents. Migrations follow expand/contract: unique indexes CONCURRENTLY, FKs added NOT VALID, then VALIDATE in a separate migration with lock_timeout. The cross-tenant id-replay fuzzer (T-100, QA) proves it.
acceptance: Given tenant A's session and tenant B's patient id, when a vitals, note, prescription, allergy, document, queue entry, appointment, invoice or consent row is inserted referencing it, then the insert fails with a foreign-key violation mapped to 404 NOT_FOUND (not 500).
Given the id-replay fuzzer (T-100) run nightly, then it finds 0 cross-tenant references.
Given production-size data (500k patients), then each VALIDATE CONSTRAINT completes without blocking writes for more than lock_timeout (3 s) and the migration lint passes.
Given the existing data, then a pre-check query finds 0 rows whose child tenant_id differs from the parent's; any found are reported before VALIDATE.

stories.title: Retried POSTs never double-charge or double-register: Idempotency-Key everywhere it matters
stories.story: As a receptionist on flaky clinic Wi-Fi I want a payment, check-in or registration that I retry to happen exactly once so that no patient is charged twice or gets two tokens.
stories.context: Retried POSTs (Wi-Fi drops, double taps) can double-charge or double-register; submitPayment has no catch (MF-26, ARCH-25, FE-11). This story adds a shared IdempotencyFilter and an idempotency_keys table: for endpoints annotated @Idempotent (payments, check-in, registration, booking, refunds, Rx sign, and every Core /internal/v1 command from Edge and Comms), the first request stores an in-progress row keyed by (tenant, actor, key) with a hash of method, path and body; a retry with the same key and body replays the stored status and body with Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with a different body returns 422; a concurrent duplicate while the first is in flight returns 409 IN_PROGRESS. Failed (5xx) attempts release the key. Stored responses are encrypted (they may hold PHI) and purged after 24 h. The generated api-client (Frontend) sends a UUIDv7 key per user action.
acceptance: Given a payment POST with Idempotency-Key K that succeeded, when the same request is retried with K, then the original 201 body is returned with Idempotent-Replayed: true and exactly one payment row exists.
Given two identical check-in requests with the same key arriving 5 ms apart, then exactly one queue entry is created; the loser gets 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS or the original response.
Given key K reused with a different body, then 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
Given the first attempt failed with 500, when retried with K, then it is processed again.
Given an @Idempotent endpoint called without the header, then 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED (staff-web and Edge always send it).
Given 24 h after creation, then the key row is purged by the purge job.

stories.title: Secure upload pipeline: type check, size limit, antivirus scan and tenant-scoped regional storage
stories.story: As a doctor I want patients' outside reports and photos uploaded safely so that I can rely on them in the consult without risking malware or another clinic seeing them.
stories.context: There is no binary upload, object store or file handling anywhere (MF-23, F-19, NB-292); this must exist before any upload feature ships (EP19, DOC-08, DENT-02, GYN-02). The pipeline: the client asks Core for an upload slot (purpose, declared type and size), gets a pre-signed PUT to a quarantine bucket in the cell's region, then calls complete. A worker sniffs magic bytes (allow-list: PDF, JPEG, PNG, HEIC converted to JPEG, later DICOM), enforces size (20 MB default), strips EXIF location, scans with ClamAV in the cell, computes SHA-256, and moves clean files to the tenant prefix of the regional bucket (server-side encryption with the tenant key once PLT-045 lands). Infected or mismatched files are quarantined and the uploader and owner are told. Inbound WhatsApp media from Comms Gateway enters the same pipeline.
acceptance: Given a PDF of 3 MB, when uploaded and completed, then it becomes available within 30 s p95 with status 'available' and a stored SHA-256.
Given a file whose magic bytes are an executable but declared as PDF, then it is rejected with status 'rejected_type' and never leaves quarantine.
Given the EICAR test file, then status 'infected', the uploader sees 'File blocked', and the owner gets an in-app alert.
Given a JPEG with GPS EXIF, then the stored version has no location metadata.
Given storage keys, then every object lives under tenant/{tenantId}/ in the tenant's region bucket and no bucket is public.
Given a 25 MB upload when the limit is 20 MB, then init returns 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE.

stories.title: Tamper-evident audit chain that does not fork, does not serialise the clinic, and is verified every night
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want the audit trail to be provably untampered, checked every night, with an alarm if anyone alters it, so that I can show an auditor that the record of who did what is intact.
stories.context: The audit hash chain (V14) finds the previous row with `SELECT row_hash FROM audit_log ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE`, which forks under concurrency, depends on RLS to scope to the tenant (global when RLS is inert), hashes created_at::text (timezone-dependent), serialises all writes of a tenant behind a backward scan (5 s), and is never verified (MF-31, ARCH-07, DP-05, SEC-27). The fix adds an audit_chain_heads row per tenant updated with `UPDATE ... RETURNING` inside the insert trigger (a short row lock per tenant, independent of RLS), hashes the UTC epoch in microseconds and canonical jsonb, versions the hash formula (hash_v=2; v1 rows verify with the old formula), runs an incremental nightly verify per tenant from the last checkpoint, writes a signed checkpoint (KMS asymmetric key) to object storage with object lock (off-box), and raises a security incident on any failure (SLO: 100%, zero budget). The trigger functions are owned by nabd_definer so the app role cannot disable them.
acceptance: Given 50 parallel audit writes for one tenant, then verify_audit_chain returns intact (no fork) (AuditChainConcurrencyTest).
Given writes for 10 tenants in parallel, then they do not wait on each other (p95 audit insert < 10 ms).
Given the session TimeZone is changed to Asia/Dubai, then hashes of new rows equal those computed under UTC.

Given the nightly job, then every tenant's chain is verified incrementally from its last checkpoint and a signed checkpoint (tenant, last_id, last_hash, signature) is written to the off-box bucket with object lock.
Given a superuser alters an audit row in staging, then the next verify fails, an alert pages the on-call as a security incident within 15 minutes, and the platform health screen shows the failure.
Given nabd_app, then it cannot DISABLE TRIGGER or UPDATE/DELETE audit_log (owner is nabd_migrator; functions owned by nabd_definer).

stories.title: Every read of patient data is recorded in an append-only, batch-sealed read log
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want every view of a patient's record logged with who, when, what and why so that I can answer 'who looked at this patient' and detect someone browsing records they should not.
stories.context: PHI reads are not audited at all (MF-18 High, SEC-09, F-09), which blocks DPDP, CERT-In, the owner audit screen and the patient 'who accessed my record' view. Per doc06 D8 the read log is separate from audit_log: a monthly-partitioned, append-only phi_read_log written synchronously in the request (one cheap insert, no chain), then sealed asynchronously in batches (batch hash chained to the previous batch). Online retention is 13 months pending DPO confirmation, then archive (PLT-042).

Given a request that fails (4xx/5xx), then no read row is written.

epics.title: Field encryption and key management
epics.goal: Encrypted fields are versioned and bound to their row, each tenant has its own regional data key, and enterprise customers can hold their own key.

stories.title: Encrypted fields carry a key version and are bound to their tenant and row
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want encrypted fields such as national IDs and MFA secrets tied to my clinic and to their row, with keys that can be rotated, so that one leaked key or copied ciphertext cannot expose other clinics' data.
stories.context: One global AES key (APP_CRYPTO_KEY) encrypts every tenant's national IDs and TOTP secrets across regions, with no key version and no associated data, so rotation is impossible and a ciphertext copied to another row decrypts fine (MF-20 S2 part, SEC-11, ARCH-36, F-11). This story replaces AesGcmCipher with a FieldCipher: ciphertext format = version byte + key id + 96-bit IV + ciphertext+tag; AAD = tenantId:table:column:rowId; keys come from a keyring in the secret manager with one active kid. A resumable re-encrypt job migrates existing values (staff.mfa_secret_enc, master.operators.mfa_secret_enc, owners.mfa_secret_enc, patients national id columns, idempotency response bodies) table by table with a progress checkpoint. Regional KMS with per-tenant keys follows in PLT-045.
acceptance: Given a new encrypted value, then it starts with the format version and key id and decrypts only with AAD tenantId:table:column:rowId.

Given a ciphertext copied from patient A's row to patient B's row (same tenant or another), then decryption fails and the API returns 500-free handling (field shown as unavailable, error logged without values).
Given the re-encrypt job, then all legacy values are rewritten in the new format, the job can stop and resume from its checkpoint, and a verification pass decrypts 100% of rows.
Given a new active kid in the keyring, then new writes use it and old values still decrypt; re-running the job rotates them.
Given the prod profile without a keyring, then boot fails.

stories.title: Patient asks for their data on WhatsApp and gets a complete export within the legal deadline
stories.story: As a patient I want to ask my clinic for a copy of all my data from WhatsApp or the patient web page and receive it as a secure download so that I can exercise my rights without visiting or emailing anyone.

stories.title: Erasure requests are executed safely: 48-hour notice, sectoral retention respected, nothing half-deleted
stories.story: As a patient I want my erasure request honoured for everything the clinic is not legally required to keep, with notice before it happens, so that I keep control without the clinic breaking medical-record law.
stories.context: Erasure must respect sectoral retention: medical records must be kept for legally required periods (e.g. IMC Regulations require at least 3 years in India; FRD market defaults), so 'erase' becomes: delete marketing and messaging data, withdraw processing consents, de-identify contact data where allowed, and restrict (not delete) clinical records under retention or legal hold, with a clear explanation to the patient. The engine sends a pre-erasure notice 48 h before execution (T-237 acceptance; DPDP Rules), then runs per-module ErasureHandlers in a saga with idempotent steps and a final verification. Audit and read logs are not erased (legal basis) but stop showing the patient's name once erased (pseudonymous ref). Legal hold (PLT-049) blocks execution. Must be live before 13 May 2027.

Given execution, then marketing/messaging data and non-required contact fields are deleted or de-identified, clinical records under retention are marked restricted, and a verification step confirms each module's handler reported done.
Given a module handler fails, then the saga retries idempotently and the request stays 'in_progress' with the failing step visible; no partial state is shown as completed.
Given a legal hold on the patient, then execution is blocked and the patient is told why within the due date.
Given the patient record after erasure, then staff search no longer finds the patient by name or phone, and audit views show a pseudonymous reference.
Given the completion, then the patient receives a confirmation listing what was erased and what is retained and for how long.

stories.title: Provisioning steps run exactly once, even when two operators click at the same time
stories.story: As a Nabd onboarding operator I want each provisioning step to run once and be safe to retry so that a double click or a crash never creates two tenants or a half-built clinic.
stories.context: ProvisioningService/ProvisioningStepRunner advance() has no transaction or lock, and listJobs is N+1 (MF-72, ARCH-26). The fix makes each step a compare-and-set (UPDATE master.provisioning_job_steps SET status='running' WHERE id=? AND status='queued' RETURNING ...; 0 rows -> 409), runs each step in its own transaction with idempotent effects keyed by (job_id, step_name), records compensation for rollback (V9 provisioning rollback), and replaces listJobs with one query aggregating steps. This is the base for the provisioning saga in the Control Plane (PLT-062).
acceptance: Given two concurrent advance calls on the same job, then exactly one step execution happens and the other returns 409 STEP_ALREADY_RUNNING.
Given a crash after a step's effect but before marking done, then a retry detects the existing effect (idempotency key) and marks it done without duplicating.
Given 200 jobs, then listJobs runs one query and returns in < 200 ms.
Given a failing step, then rollback compensations run in reverse order and the job ends rolled_back.

Given suspend or offboard, then a second operator must approve, the owner is notified, and the cell revokes sessions (PLT-007).
